items.plan: There is no shader code: the GPU re-poses the whole scene per export pass, and accumulates. A still gets no blur on the GPU, so plain --reference must stay unblurred, and Live needs nothing. Add CLI --reference-time T (seconds), parsed near src/main.rs:683, meaning the export frame at time T. Blur applies when animation.shutter>0, !animation.is_empty() and !s.physics.enabled (Job::start makes a Sim then, so blur() is false; a physics scene should be refused for --reference-time, since the Sim is not replayed here). Without blur: render animation.apply(&s,T) plus add_flashlight. With blur: shutter_s=animation.shutter/animation.fps.max(1); build M=32 moments at t=T+((i+0.5)/M-0.5)*shutter_s, each via apply then add_flashlight. Make Scene own its Settings (s: Settings rather than &'a) and drop the Progressive lifetime. Progressive holds scenes: Vec<Scene>. Share geometry: bvh: Arc<Bvh>, reused when crate::geometry_key (main.rs:333) matches the previous moment; materials, lights and cdf rebuild per moment because intensities can animate (Bvh order is deterministic only for identical tris, so reuse only on an identical key). Sample: m=if scenes.len()>1 {(r.f()*M) as usize} else {0}, drawn right after Rng::new and only when M>1 so other renders stay bit-identical. items.gpu_code: shaders/pathtrace.hlsl:1665 (mean read at :1396, updated at :1667); value at src/render.rs:376 options.x
items.plan: In the sample loop of Progressive::pass (reference.rs:1034-1040), after radiance() (already finite and non-negative): if s.firefly>0. && k>4 {let mean=*sum/k as f32; let l=lum(c); c*=(s.firefly*lum(mean).max(0.05)/l.max(1e-6)).min(1.)}; *sum+=c. lum uses 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722. Use absolute k (0-based), so the running mean is exactly the GPU's and pass splits stay bit-identical. Difference from the GPU, accepted: sampling.x is the count at frame start, so at --spp 4 the GPU starts clamping at sample 8, not 5. Remove the need at reference.rs:34. Fix tools/oracle.py: the GPU command appends --set firefly=0 after the user's sets (oracle.py:109) while the CPU gets none, so a scene or --set with firefly>0 would compare clamped CPU with unclamped GPU once the refusal goes. Put firefly=0 before the user's --set on BOTH commands. The clamp's bias depends on each sample's radiance distribution, which differs between the two estimators, so exact agreement is not expected: treat a GPU/CPU ratio as a report, not a gate. Update the refusal text and docs, since the reference is no longer clamp-free when a scene asks for the clamp.

items.plan: Keep the reference's own sampler (an independent estimator is its purpose) but give it the table's meaning. In reference.rs replace Scene.lights: Vec<usize> with `enum Light { Tri(usize), Sphere { c: Vec3, r: f32, le: Vec3 }, Sun { d: Vec3, om: f32, le: Vec3, hidden: bool } }`, keep `cdf`, and add `tri_light: Vec<u32>` per BVH triangle (0 = none, else entry + 1), which replaces the binary_search in light_pdf. Build it in Scene::new: for each `crate::lighting::analytic(s)` take l = crate::lighting::emitted(&materials[a.material]); power = 4*PI*r*r*lum(l) for a sphere, lum(l)*PI*om*(2-om)*a.area for a sun (same numbers as emitter_table); skip power <= 0. Sphere triangles (material matches an entry) set tri_light to the sphere's entry and are not added as triangles. Other triangles stay area*lum; skip lum <= 0 and area < 1e-10 as emitter_table does (today the code keeps black ones with a 1e-6 floor). The spot's cone power factor is optional because it only changes variance. Add `p_env: f32` to Scene: 0 without an environment, 1 with one and no lights, else 0.5 (later the SDF group extends this). Every light pdf in NEE and in the hit and miss weights is multiplied by (1 - p_env). sample_light returns (ld, le, pl, limit) instead of dist. Port nee_limit for triangles: max(0.0002, len - min(0.5*len, 0.0006 / max(|c|, 0.02))), with c = dot(ln, ld). This replaces `dist - 2e-3`, which is the fixed margin engine-notes 'Grazing shadow rays' removed from the GPU because it lost light at grazing angles. Also add `ng` to Surface (geometric normal flipped toward the ray) and take the shadow origin as p + ng*0.0003, as line 1607 does; today it uses the shading normal.

items.plan: The profile needs no new parsing: lighting::materials already resolves files and 'beam:' specs through ies::profile and packs them, so 'beam:' works as soon as the record is decoded. Add to reference.rs `ies_sample(m, i)`: k = i/3; v = layers[k] for k<4, sheen[k-4] for k<8, base_scale[k-8] for k<12, surface_scale[k-12] for k<16, medium[k-16] for k<19, else phase[0]; result = (((v as u32) >> (8*(i%3))) & 255) as f32 / 255. In `spot()`, test flag 16384 first and return ies_profile; a spot with a profile has no flag 32, and the profile replaces the cone. Both hit and NEE paths already call spot through `emitted`, with the cosine as the GPU has it. Trap in `unsupported`: an IES light's packed samples sit in layers, sheen and surface_scale, so the checks for clear coats (layers[0]), anisotropy (layers[3]), sheen and thin films (surface_scale[2]) report false refusals for any IES scene. In Scene::accept (reference.rs:651) use `self.s.glass_shadow || integrator != 0`, with the integrator passed per pixel because of battle mode.
(2) Portals. trace crosses them; walk_step does not, so a portal renders as its plain surface in BDPT and PM (bigger-on-the-inside is 8% off, roadmap 'no portals'). Beam splitters are handled in both.
(3) Shadow catcher and ground projection live only in trace (env_ground, background_dir). escape() uses plain environment_radiance. Gate both CPU twins on integrator==0.

(5) Path length at the bounce limit. PT loops `bounce<bounces` with NEE on the last hit, so z-scatter paths get only their NEE MIS share. BDPT uses every (s,t) with s+t-2<=D, D=min(bounces,24), so z-scatter paths keep full weight. PM limits the camera delta chain and each photon walk separately (each <=min(bounces,32)), so total length can exceed bounces. (8) Photon mapping is biased at finite passes (radius, gather slab). See the photon item.
(9) Spectral vs RGB: dispersion and exact film/grating change the image, the rest agrees to about 0.1%. See the spectral items.

items.feature: Performance on all cores
items.gpu_code: src/reference.rs:982 (cores), :1009-1055 (pass), :268-383 (Bvh::build), :739 (media Vec), :1116 (cores - 1), :920-930 (flat triangles); compare src/geometry.rs instancing in the GPU's BLAS path
items.plan: Thread use is sound. Measured, preset 0, 640x400, 32 spp, taskset: 9.0 s on 1 logical CPU, 3.0 s on 4, 1.5 s on 8, 0.5 s on 28 (the timer rounds to 0.1 s, so the last ratio is rough, about 18x). Rows are handed out dynamically and each row has its own mutex, so no false sharing to fix. Gaps: (1) Scene setup is single threaded and large: at 1 spp, 64x64 with 8 runs in parallel, forest-2 took 16.5 s, forest-1 7.8 s, crowd-2 1.9 s, nearly all setup since the tracing is tiny. Instrument geometry vs. BVH, then parallelise the BVH's upper splits with thread::scope down to 2^4 subtrees, keeping node order deterministic by concatenating in subtree order. `slots: Vec<Option<Tri>>` (:281) can become an index permutation applied at the end. (2) Live's setup is not cancellable: Progressive::new has no cancel check, so a drag on a big scene stacks full BVH builds on threads. Pass `&AtomicBool` into Scene::new and bail between geometry and each subtree, and keep at most one running job in Live. (3) Priority: Live leaves one core (:1116) yet competes on low-core machines; lower the pool's priority (SetThreadPriority BELOW_NORMAL on Windows, nice via libc on Linux, both only for Live, not the CLI). On machines with 4 or fewer cores in CPU mode also keep cores-1. (4) Per-path allocation: `media` Vec (:739) allocates on the first glass hit; the stack is at most 4 deep by the shader's rule, so a fixed `[(u32,u32);4]` plus a length removes it; same results. (5) Memory: Tri is 76 bytes and geometry() flattens instances; the forest scenes flatten everything. A two-level BVH mirroring TLAS/BLAS is the real fix, large; do it only if the measured numbers after (1) still bite; texture and other groups' UV additions enlarge Tri further. (6) SIMD: Vec3 not Vec3A; packet or wide-BVH traversal only after profiling; the 4-wide BVH is an option, not a requirement. All except (5) must keep `passes_match_one_render` bits, and (1) must keep BVH traversal results equal, not node layout.

critic.order:
SCOPE NOTES. Static read only: nothing was run, including the oracle, and no files were edited. The relayed user request is about something else ("extended flashlight config when it's enabled", last attempt "too big"). This audit did not address it. It still needs doing as UI work after this, compactly: Flashlight fields exist in src/scene.rs:682-713 and the Scene tab already shows them under the checkbox per the notes, so please clarify with the owner what "extended" should add.

COVERAGE CHECK. Every material flag bit (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, bits 8-10, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384), every cbuffer Frame field and every Settings, Material, Fog, Flashlight, AreaLight and Object field is either in the team's list, display-only, physics-only or added above, apart from these gaps: scene_info bits 4-5 (mis_mode), and flags that exist but are not reachable from reference (bits 8 and 64, the refusal hole). Team statuses I would keep: stars and moon are not-needed because sky.rs bakes them into the map (no HLSL reference), so they arrive with the atmosphere map, though they do change the image. Tilt-shift (projection 4) is inside the DoF item. Biggest theme missed: the refusal list has holes and the CLI skips time-driven state, so a scene can render wrong with no error, which undermines every parity claim until fixed.

STRUCTURE. Do the split first as pure moves in a separate commit, with no behaviour change (passes_match_one_render and oracle identical). src/reference/mod.rs: public API, unsupported, run. progressive.rs: Progressive, Live. prepare.rs: settings to frame copy. bsdf.rs: eval_bsdf, fresnel, GGX, later coat, sheen, anisotropy, film, grating. bvh.rs: BLAS and TLAS. scene.rs: Scene::new, Surface, visibility rules. lights.rs: emitter list, sample_light, MisMode. camera.rs: dispatcher. textures.rs. env.rs: HDRI, sky, split sun, ground, catcher. media.rs: dielectric stack, fog, tracking. sdf.rs. spectral.rs. integrators/{path, bdpt, photon, battle}.rs. aov.rs: LPE and AOVs. display.rs: CPU display transform. One feature per commit, each removing its refusal, adding oracle coverage and a notes line. Each integrator takes a Scene and shares a Vertex-level shade function, so BDPT and photons do not get their own copies of the BSDF rules.

ORDER.
0. Trust: refusal holes; reference::prepare (time state, flashlight, rods); f64 sums; resolve the shape-material-matrix block; owner decision on coplanar contacts.
1. Split into modules (pure move).
2. Foundations: hit frame; two-level BVH; emitter list semantics and one-sided and hidden rules; MisMode; camera dispatcher; map of integrator rules.
3. Cheap image features on those: firefly clamp, projections, DoF, sphere and sun lights, IES, flashlight, portals, beam splitters, real lens and dispersion.
4. Materials: texture store, box mapping, mesh UVs and tangents, all maps, alpha and blend, ray-cone LOD decision, then coat, sheen, anisotropy, thin film, RGB gratings.
5. Environment: HDRI, importance sampling, split sun, ground, catcher, physical sky map and sun.
6. Volumes: fog box, shadow transmittance, object media, chromatic, heterogeneous, equiangular, nested and camera medium finish. Then SDF infrastructure (as a TLAS leaf kind), fields, metaballs, exact shapes, SDF emitters.
7. Spectral core, hero and dispersion, spectral film and gratings, measured spectra. After 4 and 6, since it touches every BSDF and medium.
8. Other estimators and outputs: AOVs and LPE, BDPT plus splats, photon mapping, battle mode.
9. App: display transform, light painting then motion blur, save and export, denoiser, no-RT D3D12 device and display-only Gpu, then Vulkan, --cpu mode and fallback, interactive use, script and critique, silhouettes and freeze, ball and scene thumbnails, convergence graph, self-test coverage throughout.

Reasons for the less obvious placements: two-level BVH comes before SDF and interactive work; light painting comes before motion blur; AOVs before LPE since they share the buffers; display transform before every file and thumbnail item.
